argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than clean certification. The admissible record supports aggregate launch readiness and supports certification only if the unresolved fraud dispute review weakness is explicitly disclosed in the model card for the named launch use case. The same record does not support treating the draft runbook as an approved mitigation or treating the current model-card draft as already compliant. The audit concern is therefore best resolved as caveated compliance rather than escalation: certification can be defended on a risk-weighted basis if the packet is limited to certification with explicit disclosure, not caveat-free certification on the current draft text.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The admissible basis for minimizing escalation is that the record already supports a bounded compliance path: certify with explicit disclosure and ongoing monitoring, rather than escalate as though only rejection were supportable.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy text is the limiting rule here. Certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence shows neither: the weakness remains current, and the runbook is still draft with TBD owner and threshold. That means the draft runbook cannot remove the disclosure requirement. At the same time, the policy note says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. On this record, the compliant theory is certification paired with disclosure of the current limitation, not omission of the limitation and not reliance on draft monitoring as substitute approval.
concessions: The current model-card draft is not yet aligned with the admissible record because it says there are no known material limitations.
The draft mitigation runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for an approved mitigation because the owner and alert threshold are still TBD.
The current record does not support clean certification without first curing the disclosure defect or producing an approved alternative risk treatment.
